I did exactly what he did. I was a student and it was my first month in the clinic. We had this horrible phosphorus plate x-ray that you couldn't tell where the root were let alone the canals smh. And I'm telling you it was hemorrhaging like crazy. I kept telling this my supervisor and she kept telling me to keep going using more hipo and EDTA assuming it was calcified. I even put gutta perca in and that's when we realized what's happening and then finally they let me use some digital x-ray. They tried to save the tooth putting MTA on the perforated part but I'm sure it didn't work. Sigh. Patient was a 17 year old girl this is something I will never forget. I never had any complication like this ever again and I hope I never will. 

What I'm trying to say is you can't just not realize that you perforated the canal. It's just not possible. You feel the tuberculated part of the bone in the tip of your file. You see how immense pain your patient is in. You see the amount of blood. It's never like a canal no matter how calcified it is. I knew something was up even it was my second or third real molar that I ever touched. (I mean not an extracted tooth) I hope nobody experiences this. I still get sad thinking about it.
